MASSIVE GLORY: Near the 50 Metres was inconvenienced when crowded between SETANTA and PERFECT PAIRING.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
STAR BROSE: Raced keenly in the early stages and near the 1000 Metres was steadied to avoid VIEW ALL THINGS.  Sent for sampling post-race.
GOLDEN FORTUNE: B Avdulla reported that his mount was under pressure on the Home Turn and gave ground in the Home Straight but could offer no explanation for the horse’s disappointing performance.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
LUCKY SECRET: Noted to have blood in the mouth at the Start, was examined by the Veterinary Officer and passed suitable to race.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
SHARPEN BRIGHT: K Teetan stated that the instructions were to hold a more forward position.  He said despite riding his mount along in the early stages it failed to show sufficient pace to hold an on-pace position.
BRIGHT INHERITANCE: Bumped near the 250 Metres.  Near the 200 Metres was crowded between GOLDEN FORTUNE and PERFECT PAIRING which shifted in.
OCEAN IMPACT: From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Near the 1450 Metres became unbalanced when bumped by SPLENDID FORCE which shifted in.  Held up between the 500 Metres and the 300 Metres.  Near the 150 Metres became unbalanced when crowded between SPLENDID FORCE and COOL BLUE (S Osborne) which shifted out when held up behind SETANTA.  S Osborne was advised to exercise more care.  L Hewitson stated that his instructions were to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages.  Trainer D J Whyte stated that the intention was to hold a midfield position but the horse settled further back in the field than intended.  He added he issued those instructions as OCEAN IMPACT has run its best races when being ridden conservatively in the early stages.
VIEW ALL THINGS: Prior to the running of the event Trainer W K Mo advised that the intention was to ride the horse where comfortable with cover as it was stepping up in distance and is a recorded "roarer”.  M Chadwick stated that when caught wide in the early stages he was obliged to settle slightly further back than he had intended to ensure that he was able to obtain cover.  Leaving the 600 Metres was eased when racing tight to the inside of SPLENDID FORCE which had commenced a forward move.
COOL BLUE: Slow to begin.  Between the 400 Metres and the 300 Metres was held up for clear running and was then shifted to the outside of BRIGHT INHERITANCE near the 250 Metres to obtain clear running.  Approaching the 150 Metres became held up behind SETANTA and as a result shifted out and made contact with OCEAN IMPACT, resulting in COOL BLUE not being able to obtain clear running until near the 100 Metres.
SPLENDID FORCE: From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Near the 1450 Metres shifted in and made contact with OCEAN IMPACT.  Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.
PERFECT PAIRING: Between the 350 Metres and the 250 Metres had difficulty obtaining clear running.  When being shifted to the inside of MASSIVE GLORY near the 250 Metres made contact with BRIGHT INHERITANCE.
SHINYU KOKOROE: K Teetan reported that his mount obtained a favourable run during the event but finished the race off only fairly under pressure in the Home Straight and was disappointing.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
VIEW OF COSMOS: Prior to the running of the event Trainer C H Yip confirmed that from the outside barrier he had instructed for the horse to be ridden in a conservative manner in the early stages.  He said he issued those instructions as VIEW OF COSMOS had raced disappointingly at its most recent start when it held a more forward position.  J Orman stated that after shifting his mount behind runners in the early stages the horse did not travel well throughout the event.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
POWER PATCH: E C W Wong stated that the instructions were to hold a midfield position as connections were of the view there was good pace engaged in the event.  Trainer K L Man stated that the only explanation he could offer for the horse’s disappointing performance was that it had not appreciated racing on the All Weather surface.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  Sent for sampling post-race.
CELESTIAL STRIDER: Jumped awkwardly and lost ground.  Sent for sampling post-race.
SWAGGER BRO: S Osborne reported that after commencing well her mount failed to travel throughout the event and she was obliged to ride it along to maintain its position.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
THOUSAND CUPS: Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
TURF PHOENIX: The Veterinary Surgeon reported that TURF PHOENIX was lame in its right front leg after the race.  Before being allowed to race again, TURF PHOENIX will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
VULCANUS: Prior to the running of the event Trainer Y S Tsui confirmed that he had instructed H T Mo to take up a forward position to take advantage of its inside barrier draw.  Shifted out on jumping and was bumped.
JUICY DRAGON: Near the 700 Metres was steadied to avoid HAYDAY which shifted out making the turn.
SPARKLING FELLOW: Near the 450 Metres was hampered when bumped by GOOD LUCK HAPPY which shifted out.
FLYING HUNTER: A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
HAYDAY: Between the 450 Metres and the 350 Metres was taken back when held up behind KANSAS as KANSAS commenced to give ground.  Over the concluding stages could not be ridden out when held up behind SPARKLING FELLOW.  Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her instructions were to go forward but not necessarily lead.  She said in the early stages she rode her mount along to comply with her instructions and when other runners showed superior pace HAYDAY settled in a handy position.
KANSAS: Near the 700 Metres was taken wider by KING’S ARROW which improved to the outside of PEJIBAYE.  KANSAS then raced wide and without cover thereafter.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race which included an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse’s trachea.  Before being allowed to race again, KANSAS will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
KA YING RADIANCE: Prior to the running of the event Trainer D A Hayes confirmed that from a wide barrier he had instructed M F Poon to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages as KA YING RADIANCE had performed well when ridden in this manner previously.  From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
KING'S ARROW: L Hewitson advised that his instructions were to go forward.  He said throughout the middle stages he was disadvantaged by having to follow the leader PEJIBAYE which had led the event inside of standard time and this resulted in KING’S ARROW finishing the race off fairly over the final 200 Metres.  Trainer B Crawford confirmed the instructions and stated that he issued those instructions to take advantage of the inside barrier.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  Sent for sampling post-race.
VIGOR HAPPINESS: Prior to the running of the event Trainer Y S Tsui confirmed that he had instructed H T Mo to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages from the outside barrier.  He said he issued those instructions as the horse had raced disappointingly at its most recent starts when ridden in a more forward position.  From the outside barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
APEX GLORY: When questioned Z Purton stated that the intention was to go forward.  He said after being loaded into the starting gates APEX GLORY was fractious and as the start was effected bounded and lost ground.  He said after being positioned at the back of the field he intended to ride the horse with cover behind SHANDONG SPIRIT, however, APEX GLORY raced keenly and refused to settle.  He said as a result when BRING ME HOME improved three wide near the 900 Metres he was obliged to follow that runner, however, APEX GLORY continued to race keenly during the middle stages.  He added after entering the Home Straight he improved to the outside of BRING ME HOME but his mount responded only fairly to his riding and, in his opinion, was particularly disappointing over the final 200 Metres when it commenced to give ground.  Trainer K L Man stated the horse was disadvantaged by losing ground at the start and also racing too keenly.  A warning was placed on the barrier manners of APEX GLORY. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of APEX GLORY, a last start winner, was considered disappointing.  Before being allowed to race again, APEX GLORY will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.  Sent for sampling post-race.
BRING ME HOME: Jumped only fairly.  Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  Noted to have sustained a small abrasion to the right hind leg after the race.  Sent for sampling post-race.
PUDDING GOGO: From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
GOLDEN TRIUMPH: Lay in in the Home Straight.
HAPPY BRETHREN: K C Leung reported that his mount raced keenly in the lead, particularly with LITTLE MONSTER being positioned to his outside.  He said as a result the horse was unable to finish the race off in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
HIGH RISE VICTORY: Jumped only fairly.  S Osborne advised that she was instructed to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages as HIGH RISE VICTORY had not been finishing its races off when ridden in a forward position.  Trainer C H Yip confirmed the instructions issued.
SHAMZ: Jumped only fairly.  Between the 400 Metres and the 300 Metres had difficulty obtaining clear running.
AGENDA: B Avdulla reported that in the Home Straight his mount hung in and proved difficult to ride out.
FULL OF FORTUNE: Shifted in abruptly at the start and made heavy contact with GHORGAN.
BLING BLING GENIUS: Shifted in abruptly at the start and was bumped.
MEGA MASTERMIND: Near the 150 Metres raced tight between POLAR PATCH and FRANCIS MEYNELL, both of which shifted ground.
ROSEWOOD FLEETFOOT: Shifted out slightly at the start and became unbalanced when it made contact with GHORGAN.  J Orman stated that his mount finished the race off in a one-paced manner and would appreciate being stepped up in distance.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
GHORGAN: Prior to the running of the event Trainer J Cummings advised that he had instructed L Ferraris to ride the horse where comfortable.  Jumped awkwardly and then was checked at the start when crowded between ROSEWOOD FLEETFOOT which shifted out slightly and FULL OF FORTUNE which shifted in abruptly despite the efforts of its rider.  In the early stages raced keenly and for some distance near the 1100 Metres became badly unbalanced when it got its head up when being steadied to avoid POLAR PATCH.  GHORGAN continued to race keenly throughout the middle stages.
LUCKY YEAR: Raced wide and without cover from the 800 Metres.  Sent for sampling post-race.
BIG BIG WORLD: Prior to the running of the event Trainer K H Ting confirmed that from a wide barrier he had instructed K C Leung to ride the horse in a positive manner, preferably with cover.
GORGEOUS VICTORY: Between the 400 Metres and the 200 Metres was held up for clear running.  Sent for sampling post-race.
AUTOMATED: On jumping was bumped on the hindquarters by POLAR PATCH.
FRANCIS MEYNELL: K Teetan reported that near the 150 Metres when GORGEOUS VICTORY improved to his inside his mount hung out and as a consequence he was obliged to stop riding and straighten it.
POLAR PATCH: On jumping became unbalanced when bumped by BLING BLING GENIUS which shifted in abruptly.  Leaving the 1100 Metres, when racing keenly, was steadied to avoid AUTOMATED (R Kingscote) which shifted in when not clear.  R Kingscote was advised to exercise more care.  After being crossed by AUTOMATED, POLAR PATCH was then allowed to stride forward where it obtained a position behind the lead.
LADY'S LOVE: Z Purton stated that his mount failed to travel well throughout the event and disappointed in its response to his riding in the Home Straight.  Trainer C W Chang stated that the horse had pleased him leading into the race and he expected it to perform well but could offer no excuse for its performance.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of LADY’S LOVE, a last start winner, was considered disappointing.  Before being allowed to race again, LADY’S LOVE will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
CALL ME SPARKLE: J Orman reported that he was instructed to go forward but, in his opinion, the horse may be better suited by being ridden in a more conservative manner as it failed to respond to his riding in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
FIND MY LOVE: M L Yeung stated that from a wide barrier he was instructed to take up a forward position.  He said when unable to cross runners to his inside he was obliged to race wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  Trainer D J Whyte confirmed that with the horse stepping up in distance he had instructed Jockey Yeung to go forward.
BEAUTY AWARD: Jumped awkwardly.  Sent for sampling post-race.
CALIFORNIA WAVES: B Avdulla stated that from the outside barrier he was instructed to hold a handy position with cover.  He said although CALIFORNIA WAVES commenced well it did not show the necessary pace to hold a more forward position and when caught wide approaching the 1200 Metres he elected to ease his mount to ensure that he obtained cover.  He added as a consequence CALIFORNIA WAVES settled further back than what had been intended.
SHOTGUN: Noted to have lost its right front plate after the race.
MIGHTY FIGHTER: Between the 400 Metres and the 300 Metres was held up for clear running.  Leaving the 300 Metres was shifted to the outside of MY WYNDFALL and LUCKY MAN to obtain clear running.  Sent for sampling post-race.
SUPERB KID: Slow to begin.  Shifted to the inside of LADY’S LOVE approaching the 200 Metres to continue into clear running.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
PERFECTDAY: Finished tailed out.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race revealed that the horse was displaying an irregular heart rhythm.  Before being allowed to race again, PERFECTDAY will be required to perform satisfactorily in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
TAGLINE: Prior to the running of the event Trainer M Newnham confirmed that he had instructed L Ferraris to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages to offset the wide barrier.  From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  When questioned L Ferraris confirmed that the instructions were to settle back in the field.  He said after following PROFESSIONAL LAD during the event he considered improving between PROFESSIONAL LAD and PANACEA making the Home Turn.  He said when PROFESSIONAL LAD shifted out leaving the 500 Metres to improve he then elected to improve to the inside of PROFESSIONAL LAD.  He added after making ground near the 400 Metres he then was not able to place full vigour to his mount as he was concerned that PERFECTDAY, which was giving ground, may shift in and interfere with his mount and therefore he was required to ride with caution between the 400 Metres and the 250 Metres.  He said when PERFECTDAY shifted out whilst giving ground near the 250 Metres his mount became slightly unbalanced when bumped by PERFECTDAY after which he was able to apply full pressure to TAGLINE.  He added TAGLINE finished the race off well, however, he was of the opinion his mount may also have appreciated the surface with more give in it.
TITAN PEGASUS: Jumped awkwardly and then was bumped by STORM MIRROR which shifted in.  C L Chau reported that he had some difficulty obtaining clear running near the 400 Metres when held up behind PERFECTDAY.  He said after obtaining clear running shortly after TITAN PEGASUS was one-paced to the finish of the event.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
CHIU CHOW SPIRIT: Passing the 50 Metres was eased when unable to continue to improve between PANACEA and MONARCH COUNTY, both of which shifted ground.
PRECISION TIME: Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.
STORM MIRROR: Shifted in at the start and was bumped.  C Y Ho stated that he was satisfied with his mount’s performance, particularly stepping up to Class 3 grade.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  Sent for sampling post-race.
MONARCH COUNTY: Near the 100 Metres shifted in, resulting in its rider S Osborne having to stop riding and straighten.  Sent for sampling post-race.
KING PATCH: Shifted in at the start and made contact with ZHUANG YUAN GLORY.
ZHUANG YUAN GLORY: Jumped only fairly and then was bumped at the start.
PANACEA: Prior to the running of the event Trainer P F Yiu confirmed that from the outside barrier he had instructed H T Mo to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages.  From the outside barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Sent for sampling post-race.
BEAUTY JOY: B Avdulla reported that his mount was obliged to race wide and without cover for the majority of the event and as a result was unable to finish the race off in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
NUMBERS: On jumping became unbalanced when it made contact with SILVERY BREEZE after being taken out by CALIFORNIATOTALITY.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
SKY JEWELLERY: In the early stages got its head up when being shifted across behind runners from a wide barrier.  A Atzeni stated that after settling back in the field he was steadied to avoid BEAUTY JOY near the 700 Metres when BEAUTY JOY gave ground.  He said from this point SKY JEWELLERY did not travel well thereafter and found it difficult to make up ground from back in the field, particularly with the early and middle stages being run outside of standard time.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of SKY JEWELLERY was considered disappointing as compared to its previous race starts.  Before being allowed to race again, SKY JEWELLERY will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.  Sent for sampling post-race.
MASSIVE SOVEREIGN: From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Approaching the 700 Metres improved between BEAUTY JOY and SILVERY BREEZE.  A short distance later SILVERY BREEZE then shifted out, resulting in MASSIVE SOVEREIGN having to be steadied when crowded between BEAUTY JOY and SILVERY BREEZE.  On the Home Turn was held up behind BEAUTY JOY and as a result was shifted to the inside to obtain clear running.  Between the 400 Metres and the 250 Metres was held up for clear running.
SPEED DRAGON: Bumped at the start and then was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Between the 400 Metres and the 300 Metres had difficulty obtaining clear running.  C L Chau was found guilty of a careless riding charge for causing interference near the 100 Metres (see LE ZONDA).  Sent for sampling post-race.
GENTLEMEN LEGACY: Noted to have sustained a small abrasion to the left hind leg after the race.  Sent for sampling post-race.
LE ZONDA: Jumped awkwardly and lost ground.  C L Chau (SPEED DRAGON) was found guilty of a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that near the 100 Metres he allowed his mount to shift in when insufficiently clear of LE ZONDA, resulting in LE ZONDA losing its rightful running and having to be steadied and also LE ZONDA then shifting in across the running of CALIFORNIATOTALITY which was steadied.  C L Chau was suspended from riding in races for a period to commence on Sunday, 29 November 2026 and to expire on Thursday, 3 December 2026 on which day he may resume race riding (2 Hong Kong racedays).  In addition, Jockey Chau was fined $60,000.  In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered his poor race riding record.
SILVERY BREEZE: On jumping was checked when crowded between SPEED DRAGON and NUMBERS which was taken out.
CALIFORNIATOTALITY: Shifted out on jumping and made contact with NUMBERS.  Near the 150 Metres was hampered when crowded between NUMBERS and MASSIVE SOVEREIGN which was racing tight to the inside of LE ZONDA.  Near the 100 Metres was steadied when crowded by LE ZONDA.
THAT'S GOLD: Prior to the running of the event Trainer M Newnham confirmed that from a wide barrier he had instructed L Ferraris to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages.  From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
CELESTIAL HERO: Z Purton stated that his mount was disadvantaged by racing wide and without cover for the majority of the event and as a result finished the race off only fairly in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
AKASHVANI: Near the 1100 Metres was steadied to avoid THRIVING BROTHERS (H Bentley) which shifted in when not sufficiently clear.  H Bentley was reprimanded and advised he must ensure he is clear when shifting ground.  B Avdulla was found guilty of a careless riding charge for causing interference near the 900 Metres (see PASS LINE).  B Avdulla stated that he had intended to be slightly more forward than its previous race starts as connections were of the view there was not strong pace engaged in today’s race.  He added that when AKASHVANI jumped well he was able to hold an on-pace position.
GOLD TAOGETHER: Shortly after the start was steadied to avoid AKASHVANI (B Avdulla) which shifted in.  B Avdulla was advised to exercise more care.  Near the 150 Metres was steadied when crowded between FIT FOR BEAUTY (A Atzeni) which shifted out slightly and THAT’S GOLD (L Ferraris) which shifted in slightly.  Both A Atzeni and L Ferraris were advised to exercise more care in similar circumstances.
SUPERB SPIRIT: Near the 900 Metres lost its rightful running when being steadied.  Shifted out near the 800 Metres when being steadied to avoid FIT FOR BEAUTY and made contact with HAR HAR POWER.  Sent for sampling post-race.
HAR HAR POWER: Near the 1200 Metres was checked when crowded between FIT FOR BEAUTY which was taken out slightly by GOLDEN CHAMP (A Badel) and AKASHVANI which was taken in by THRIVING BROTHERS (H Bentley) which shifted in before being corrected.  A Badel was advised to exercise more care.  H Bentley was severely reprimanded.  Near the 800 Metres became unbalanced when bumped by SUPERB SPIRIT which shifted out.  Raced very wide and without cover for the majority of the event.
FASTOSO: From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Between the 350 Metres and the 250 Metres was held up for clear running.  Lay out over the final 200 Metres and near the 50 Metres shifted out and made contact with PASS LINE.
PAPAYA BROSE: E C W Wong stated that from the outside barrier he was instructed to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages.  He added that under pressure in the Home Straight PAPAYA BROSE finished the race off only fairly.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
PASS LINE: Jumped only fairly.  Shortly after the start was steadied when crowded between SUPERB SPIRIT and HAR HAR POWER, both of which shifted ground.  B Avdulla (AKASHVANI) was found guilty of a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that near the 900 Metres he allowed his mount to shift in when not clear of FIT FOR BEAUTY, resulting in FIT FOR BEAUTY being taken in onto SUPERB SPIRIT, resulting in SUPERB SPIRIT losing its running and having to be steadied and also shifting in and crowding the running of PASS LINE, causing PASS LINE to be checked.  B Avdulla was suspended from riding in races for one Hong Kong raceday to be conducted on Wednesday, 18 November 2026 at Happy Valley.  In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered his very good race riding record.  Bumped near the 50 Metres.
FLYING KNIGHT: When giving ground approaching the 100 Metres was steadied to avoid FASTOSO which shifted out and away from GOLDEN CHAMP.
HELENE SUPAFEELING: Withdrawn on 5.11.26 by order of the Stewards acting on veterinary advice (lame left fore) and replaced by Standby Declared Starter THAT’S GOLD.  Before being allowed to race again, HELENE SUPAFEELING will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
GRAND EAGLE: C L Chau reported that after the 600 Metres his mount became badly unbalanced when bumped heavily by CITY GOLD BANNER.  He said after this incident GRAND EAGLE did not travel well and failed to respond to his riding in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
MAJESTIC VALOUR: After the race an endoscopic examination was conducted on MAJESTIC VALOUR at the request of Trainer C S Shum.  The Veterinary Surgeon said this examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse’s trachea.  Before being allowed to race again, MAJESTIC VALOUR will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.  Sent for sampling post-race.
PEGAS: Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.
CITY GOLD BANNER: Blundered near the 850 Metres.  Near the 600 Metres commenced to race keenly and as a result got its head up when being checked to avoid YOUNG ARCHER.  In this incident CITY GOLD BANNER shifted out and made heavy contact with GRAND EAGLE.
DYNAMIC GOLF: Shortly after the start was bumped by LIFELINE EXPRESS which shifted out.  Raced keenly in the early stages and near the 900 Metres was steadied to avoid PEGAS which shifted in before being corrected by its rider.  DYNAMIC GOLF continued to race keenly for some distance thereafter.
YOUNG ARCHER: Jumped only fairly.  Sent for sampling post-race.
CONGHUA GALAXY: Jumped awkwardly and made contact with the left side of its starting gate.
TURBO GRANNY: Jumped only fairly.  Blundered near the 850 Metres and again near the 500 Metres.
LIFELINE EXPRESS: Shifted out shortly after the start and was bumped.  Approaching the 250 Metres was steadied to avoid PEGAS when disappointed for clear running between PEGAS and CITY GOLD BANNER.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
LOVE ESPRESSO: A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
HONG LOK GOLF: Shifted out at the start and made contact with BEAUTY ALLIANCE.  Near the 900 Metres was briefly crowded by MUGEN which shifted in.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
STORM RIDER: Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that it was not the intention to lead but her mount jumped well and showed superior pace and led without being pressured to do so.
AERIS NOVA: From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
MUGEN: Near the 900 Metres was steadied to avoid COLOURFUL STAR.
BEAUTY ALLIANCE: Bumped at the start.  Near the 900 Metres was steadied to avoid MUGEN.  BEAUTY ALLIANCE was then obliged to race wide and without cover thereafter.
GARRIX: Near the 800 Metres was steadied to avoid BEAUTY ALLIANCE.  R Kingscote stated that from the outside barrier his mount was obliged to settle back in the field to obtain cover.  He said in the Home Straight his mount found it difficult to make up ground, particularly with the early stages being run outside of standard time.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
